updates.title: GitHub makes Copilot in Slack and Teams generally available
updates.whatChanged: On 6 November, GitHub made @GitHub in Slack and Teams generally available. Users can ask @GitHub to investigate bugs, create issues, implement changes, and open pull requests from a conversation. In Teams, Canvas lets users review implementation plans, code changes, and previews alongside chat. Issues and pull requests identify the Slack or Teams user who started them.
updates.whyCare: You can move from a Slack or Teams discussion to a coding session without changing tools. Teams Canvas lets teammates review plans and changes together. Treat general availability as an adoption option; keep pull-request review in place.
updates.before: The Slack and Teams integration was not generally available. Teams had no Canvas flow to review plans and changes in Teams conversations.
updates.after: Users can ask @GitHub in Slack or Teams to investigate bugs, create issues, implement changes, and open pull requests. In Teams, users can review plans, code changes, and previews in Canvas alongside chat.
updates.learn: Pilot @GitHub with one team. Check repository selection and review permissions before allowing it to create pull requests from a conversation. Confirm that issues and pull requests identify the Slack or Teams user who started them.

sources.name: GitHub Changelog - @GitHub in Slack and Teams is generally available and more

updates.architectureImplication: Use Slack and Teams as managed entry points for GitHub coding-agent work. Keep repository-scoped access and normal pull-request checks in place. Use Canvas when teammates need to review plans, code changes, and previews together.
